text: What: Show directed base-to-variant relationships for the current font. How: Match an exact final suffix such as alt or ss01. Draw each base -> variant pair and produce individual OpenType substitution statements in font order. Why: A feature draft is easier to review when its name relationships are visible. Usage: Enter a suffix without the dot, Refresh, then Copy Result. Paste the statements into a chosen feature in FontLab and compile there after review. Benefit: Inspect proposed substitutions before use. The graph infers names only; it does not read, validate or compile feature code. The full text draft is retained; the scene shows at most 100 pairs. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and fontlabapp. Modeless; no font writes. text: What: Draw a star polygon in the current FontLab layer as one Undo step. How: Alternate radii in font units, with Y up. Centre the contour on half the active layer advance and half its associated master's FontMetrics cap height. Why: Start ornamental glyphs from repeatable, font-sized construction. Usage: Open a glyph. Set tips, radii in ems and rotation. Generate Preview, then Draw in Current Layer. Each Draw adds one closed contour in a new shape. Auto layers and bases of auto composites are refused. Read-back checks the new contour and verifies every pre-existing shape's geometry. Layers without an associated master are refused. Draw coordinates use whole-unit half-up rounding (ties away from zero); read-back allows 0.5 units on each new-node coordinate. A partial-write error directs you to Edit > Undo. Benefit: Create geometric artwork directly in the active glyph layer. The read-only shape preview is centred at the origin; drawing placement uses the current advance and cap height. Equal radii produce a regular polygon with twice the tip count. Positive rotation turns counterclockwise. SVG is secondary output for an external vector editor. Generate Preview, then copy the SVG text or Save New SVG to a new absolute .svg path. SVG uses a Y-down em square and contains no font metrics, anchors or hints. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and fontlabapp. Modeless panel. The App panel owns signals and completion. No painter or plugin is needed. text: Query current-font name, Unicode and modification data with trusted Python. What: Evaluate short expressions or statements on detached glyph records. How: Capture once on the UI thread with a glyph-count-scaled deadline and a Scanning label (at most 120 seconds). Build the namespace once. No worker or conversion timer is used. Why: Test report expressions without giving the query namespace native handles. Usage: Capture, enter Python, then Run or press Return. For example, [g['name'] for g in glyphs if not g['unicode']]. The unicode field is a string such as "U+0041 U+00C1"; modified is "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", or empty if unset. Select output and copy to a script or report. Capture resets local variables. Choose the query deadline: 5 seconds by default, at most 60 seconds. A Python trace guard stops Python loops and restores the earlier host trace. A loop in native code without Python line events cannot be stopped by this guard. Code that catches every exception can outlive the time limit. Benefit: Experiment with real glyph data and keep complete query results. This runs trusted code in the host process, not a security sandbox. User code can change detached data. The panel itself calls no font writer. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App glyph_catalog/draft_signals/scripting. Independent rewrite of timer-batch and owned-repl. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. No original source body is redistributed.

text: What: Report contour problems on the current font's current master. How: Inspect each glyph's contours once. List open contours, closed contours with fewer than three on-curve nodes, equal adjacent nodes and small node extents. Why: A combined report gives one repair checklist before overlap removal. Usage: Open a font. Set the minimum extent, then Refresh. Enter an absolute new JSON filename and Export to save the complete captured checklist. Benefit: A build check or another FontLab script can consume the JSON file. Small extents use node coordinates, including control points, in shape space. They are a diagnostic heuristic, not exact curve bounds. The report does not flatten components. Missing master layers are listed separately. No font data changes. Use Select glyphs with findings after activating the Font window. Scriptmix Reports > Open Contours is the master-wide variant that selects glyphs. This tool adds a combined checklist and complete JSON export for build checks. Scanning runs in small UI-thread steps; Cancel discards the entire unfinished report. Font, master, glyph order and modification-date changes reject the scan. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. text: What: Copy layers from another open font to selected current-font glyphs. How: Map source and destination layer names. Preview and confirm Overwrite, Incoming + suffix, Destination + suffix or Mask. One Copy is recorded as one Undo step in the destination. Both fonts are identified by fgId. Why: Native Paste Special uses the clipboard; this repeats explicit layer maps without switching fonts. The source is read only and glyphs must already exist. Usage: Select destination glyphs in its Font window, choose a source, enter mappings, Preview, inspect kept rows, confirm, then Copy. Benefit: Transfer outlines, anchor positions and advances across many glyphs. Components, hints, guides, metric expressions, locked/automatic layers and unsafe automatic dependants are kept. Element names, notes and transforms, contour names, node names and raw flags are retained; selection flags clear. Custom node/contour properties are refused. Anchor coordinates use App; existing pin styles stay, new pins use name-derived styles. Anchor expressions, layer metadata, links and colour marks are not copied. Units per em must match. Mask replaces the mapped layer's mask. Destination + suffix refuses master renames; existing suffix names are kept. New names cannot contain @ or # or begin with |temp|, mask, img. or bw.. Capture allows 3 seconds plus one second per selected glyph/mapping; a timeout refuses the whole preview. Apply rechecks the displayed plan. Partial failures direct you to Edit > Undo. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly, App>=0.2.150.dev0. Independent behaviour rewrite of TR-CopyLayers.py, Vassil Kateliev / Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No upstream code, comments or assets copied. Implementation: Apache-2.0.

text: What: Save and compare current-master naming and credit settings as JSON. How: Capture package naming, version, PostScript and credit text. Export a versioned snapshot. text: What: Import many current-master kerning pairs from a pasted text list. How: Read left right value lines; # begins a comment. Preview every row before Apply. Decimal values round half away from zero to whole units. Invalid rows block the entire batch. Duplicate pair lines require correction. Why: A pair list can carry different values for many glyph and class pairs. Usage: Open a font, paste the list, press Preview and inspect the table. Press Apply for one Undo step. Edit the list and Preview again for another batch. Benefit: Transfer measured pairs without creating glyphs or kerning classes. @class names must already exist on the correct side of the current master's kerning. Glyphs with automatic layers, including members of a named class, are refused by the shared FontLab editing rules. Apply checks the font, master, text and complete kerning snapshot again. Native read-back verifies the written batch. Keep the panel open for repeated imports. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Based on the author's own FontLab sample, Apache-2.0. Source: recipe.py (Kerning Pairs from Text).

text: What: Expand kerning copy rules into a current-master import list. How: Read explicit pairs once. Use A|V A|W = T|o @ -5 to copy T/o minus five units to A/V and A/W. @class names use native kerning-class notation. Every rule reads the original snapshot. No rule reads another rule's output. Why: Reuse measured pairs without manual arithmetic or repeated pair edits. Usage: Open a font. Enter rules. Build, inspect and Copy. Paste straight into Tools > Import Kerning Pair List, then Preview and Apply. Export is optional. Import uses the master that is current when you press Preview; check its status. Benefit: Keep a reproducible pair list. This panel never changes the font. Only explicit current-master pairs are read; inherited class results are not guessed. All glyphs and class sides must exist. Offsets and results must be whole units. A repeated destination or invalid row refuses the entire output. The source supports all masters, automatic glyph-to-class lookup, character tokens and arithmetic adjustments. This port keeps explicit current-master glyph or @class tokens and integer additive adjustments only. It has no All masters mode, automatic class lookup, character tokens, general arithmetic, class-file import or direct application. Use native Kerning panel > Copy Kerning From for complete-master transfers. Requires FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App >= 0.2.150.dev0. Credit: Independent behaviour rewrite of CopyKerning.py by Vassil Kateliev, Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No source code, comments, icons or preset formats are copied.

text: What: Compare selected glyph-layer measurements with one reference cell. How: Read complete equal passes of advances, outline bounds and sidebearings. text: What: Draft localized typographic family and subfamily names for a font build. How: Prefill from current-master package names, with family/style fallback. Include the resulting .fea in an AFDKO makeotf or fontmake feature file; inspect the compiled name table. This tool does not install a translation or edit the open font. Benefit: Produce build input instead of changing global application language. Export or explicitly discard edited translations before closing. Language IDs are decimal or 0x-prefixed; the tool checks range, not language registration. text: Set selected node slopes and cubic handle lengths in a non-modal panel. What: Copy a slope, use each master's italic angle, flip the slope or pivot at the top or bottom selected node. Set cubic handle proportions or Hobby tensions. How: Slope is dx/dy; selected nodes keep y. Each moved on-curve node carries its adjacent unselected handles by the same offset, including at a closed contour's wrap. Selected handles use their own slope targets. Curve modes require both segment endpoints selected. Handle rays stay fixed; Proportions measures length against the endpoint chord. Hobby uses the two endpoint tangent angles and independent positive tensions. Copy Proportions reads exactly one selected cubic. Closing cubics are included; open ends stay. Why: Contour > Align Points and Contour > Handles > Harmonize serve direct edits. This panel adds explicit reusable numbers, two handle tensions and a batch preview. Use: Select nodes, run the tool, choose the mode and inspect the table. Reload selection after changing glyphs. Each Apply is recorded as one Undo step. Benefit: Repeat the same numeric rule across selected glyphs and masters. Selection is read separately in each master. Automatic layers, shared outlines, scaled or rotated shapes and quadratic contours are kept. No node is inserted, deleted or retyped. Zero handle rays and zero chords are kept. General node conversion, retraction and Tunni editing remain native or existing tools. The preview lists each changed node's old and planned coordinates. Read-back uses the App comparison epsilon; native coordinate storage remains subject to FontLab's rounding preference. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. text: What: Scale selected glyphs with independent vertical/horizontal stem compensation. How: Each checked master row supplies two source layers, their measured stems, target stems, scale X/Y and slant. Unslant all nodes, blend X/Y independently, scale and reslant. Preview lists every glyph/master and output layer. Confirm, then Create Layers. The entire batch is recorded as one Undo step. Why: Plain scaling changes stems. Per-master stem measurements make derived small caps or superiors without changing the source masters. Usage: Select glyphs in the Font window. Use Selection, check target master rows, edit their source pairs and measurements, Preview, inspect kept rows, confirm. Benefit: Generate many compensated glyph layers in one repeatable action. Outputs are new auxiliary layers named master + suffix. Existing outputs are kept. New names cannot contain @ or # or start with |temp|. No in-place overwrite or whole-font default is provided. Preview and Apply each scan dependencies once; control edits never scan fonts. Apply rechecks the displayed plan. All nodes and controls use the same affine blend; TT contours remain quadratic, including consecutive controls and implied on-curves. First-source node names, raw flags and contour names are retained, with selection flags cleared. Advance is first-source advance times scale X. Components, transforms, automatic or locked sources, custom node/contour properties and unsafe automatic dependants are kept. Anchors, guides, hints, element metadata and metrics expressions are not copied. Source layers stay unchanged. Slant defaults to minus the current master's angle; each table row can override it. Extrapolation, boundary-fix, stem probing and saved table presets are not provided. Partial failures direct you to Edit > Undo. Setup: FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App>=0.2.150.dev0. Non-modal panel. Independent behaviour rewrite of DeltaMachine.py, Vassil Kateliev / Karandash Type Foundry, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig The small arithmetic helper reuses the Apache-2.0 Stem Blend implementation. No TypeRig code, private identifiers, comments or assets copied. Capture allows 3 seconds plus one second per selected glyph/master. A timeout refuses the whole preview; select fewer glyphs. Read-back allows coordinate changes up to 1e-3 units. Advance is checked against its detached value read immediately after the native setter applies the current rounding preference, with the same tolerance. The coordinate tolerance is measured in FontLab 9: coordinates drift 1.2e-5..1.6e-5 after Redo and up to 5e-4 after save and reopen (live reports 16 and 17).

text: What: Write a stem-compensated blend into a new layer of the current glyph. How: Divide target stems by scale to choose independent X/Y interpolation fractions. Unslant, blend, scale and reslant. The final stems match the typed measurements when the source stems interpolate linearly. Why: Make scaled lettering at a requested stem size without changing masters. Usage: Open a glyph. Choose two source layers. Enter measured source and target stems and scale factors. Build, inspect the output name, then Create Layer. The layer name is Stem x ( ), for example Stem 75x60 (Light). Names containing @ or #, starting with |temp|, or matching a master name are refused. An existing layer name is refused. Each new layer is recorded as one Undo step through App history. The new layer becomes the active layer. Benefit: Keep native font-unit geometry without an artwork import transform. The angle starts at minus the current master's italic angle; positive means that the top moves right. Refresh Sources reloads layer choices and the angle. Targets divided by scale must lie between the measured source stems. Equal stems, components, shape transforms and incompatible paths are refused. TrueType off-curves stay quadratic, including implied on-curve midpoints. The new layer keeps the first source's advance. Anchors, hints, node flags and other source metadata are not copied. Automatic-layer owners and bases of automatic composites are kept unchanged and named in the refusal message. Copy SVG is secondary artwork only. SVG import may rescale or reposition it; no SVG import preserves scale by this tool's guarantee. No stored axis setup, extrapolation or batch target baking is provided. Use native Font > Generate Instance for native instance generation. Requires FontLab 9, Python 3.11, Fly and App >= 0.2.150.dev0. Credit: Independent behaviour rewrite of Delta.py and DeltaNew.py by Vassil Kateliev, TypeRig, kateliev/TypeRig, MPL-2.0. https://github.com/kateliev/TypeRig No source code, comments, icons or preset formats are copied. Read-back allows coordinate changes up to 1e-3 units. Advance is checked against its detached value read immediately after the native setter applies the current rounding preference, with the same tolerance. text: write_metric ( font : Any , name : str , metric : str , value : float , * , layer : str | None = None , undo_name : str | None = None ) -> bool Set metric ( lsb , rsb or width ) of glyph name to value . One font.edit_glyph(name, layer=<layer>, undo_name=<undo_name>) per call. layer defaults to font.defaultLayerName ; a different layer reads its metrics from font.getLayer(layer) . undo_name defaults to "TMetrics: <LSB|RSB|width> <name>" . LSB shifts contours, components and anchors horizontally and grows the width by the same amount, keeping RSB; RSB and width change only the advance. Return False (no write) when the value already holds; raise ValueError for an unknown field, a non-finite value, a missing glyph or a sidebearing of an empty glyph, and TypeError for a font without edit_glyph .

text: Shared kernel of the scripts that make new glyphs from copies of existing ones. What: Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies plan one new glyph per selected source glyph and copy its contours, transformed, into every master. This module holds the parts that were byte-identical in the three scripts: survey_with plans one Row per selected name with the script's naming rule. It lists and skips a repeated target, a missing source, a target that exists, a source layer that cannot be copied ( source_problem ) and, without the user's consent, a target that can make FontLab rebuild automatic glyphs ( Row.rebuild ). create makes the planned glyphs through fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs : each glyph with its master widths, then all contours in one Undo step, then a read-back. panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the shared panel of the three scripts (a fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.model panel with a source table and the rebuild consent tick). How: a job is (new name, [(master, contours, advance)]) ; the script's prepare builds it with fontlabapp.contours.copy.copy_contours . Undo: glyph_creation.UNDO_TEXT . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads in panel_type() and fontlab in create . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.glyphs.copies as glyph_copies rows = glyph_copies.survey_with(package, names, naming, facts, allow_rebuild) result = glyph_copies.create(package, jobs, "Small Caps", facts, allow_rebuild=True)

text: Create new glyphs through FontLab's own Add Glyph command, then fill them in one step. What: the Contours creator scripts (Placeholder Glyphs, Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures, Tabular Figure Copies) make new glyphs. create_glyphs does it in this order: Refuse before any change ( ValueError ): a name listed twice, a name that exists now, a name that can make FontLab rebuild an automatic glyph ( auto_candidates ) without the user's consent, a Glyph window as the active canvas ( edit_guards.require_history_scope , FontLab issue 8573: measured on 9790, Undo stays disabled for the new glyphs and their outlines there). Read queued native glyph updates for disclosure (FontLab issue 8537); never clear them. Read the signature of every automatic layer ( auto_signatures ). For each new glyph, call the fontpr tool set_glyph(create=True) with the name, one layer per master with its advance width, the code points and optional components ( NewGlyph.components , Part ; glyph_data ). The components are checked after the call. FontLab runs its undoable Add Glyph command ( commAddGlyph ) for it. Optionally fill the new layers in ONE history.commit(..., operation="geometry") that declares the new layers and glyphs. Read back: the caller's read_back texts, then one text per automatic layer whose signature changed ( auto_changes ). User text for the Undo shape: UNDO_TEXT ("Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step."). This module makes no claim about what Undo restores. Why: flPackage.addGlyph is a raw insert. It runs no command and records no history (source: flpackage.cpp:18526-18532 ), and it skips ensureComplete . set_glyph creates the glyph the way FontLab's own tools do (source: mcptools_source.cpp:144-172 ); the command runs synchronously and clears the queued glyph updates ( flhistorycontroller.cpp:1818-1914 ). Glyport creates glyphs the same way. This module never calls addGlyph and never writes a FontGate record. The Add Glyph command re-resolves the default-recipe automatic composites of the font ( commAddGlyph::updateAutoGlyphs , fl#8512). FontLab gives no Python call that predicts a default recipe, so auto_candidates is a conservative guess: automatic layers without an own recipe whose glyph name shares a dotted suffix segment with the new name (a new e.sc can change eacute.sc ). The script lists them ("may rebuild auto eacute.sc") and creates such a glyph only after the user ticks REBUILD_LABEL . The after-write check ( auto_changes ) stays. Automatic layers are never notified. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; fontpr loads when create_glyphs runs. Offline tests prove the call order, not native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.glyphs.creation as glyph_creation specs = [glyph_creation.NewGlyph("h.sc", (("Regular", 450),))] done = glyph_creation.create_glyphs(package, specs, "Small Caps", facts, fill=fill)

text: capture ( * , deadline : float | None = None ) -> Any Read the glyph names, Unicode values and dates of the current font. What: return an immutable fontlabapp.qt.tables.filter.model.Table with the columns "Glyph name", "Unicode" and "Modified" in font order. rows holds (name, "U+0041 U+00C1", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss") tuples and epochs holds the modification instants ( None when unset). How: the private _glyph_catalog_native.capture reads the whole font twice from FontGate records mapped by package.findFgId . It never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph . A change between the reads rejects the whole result. Use: call it on the main UI thread. deadline is a time.monotonic() instant; the default budget is two seconds. It raises ValueError with no open font or a changed font, TimeoutError after the deadline and RuntimeError off the main thread. It writes nothing. Native preservation is not proved by offline tests.

text: auto_candidates ( package : Any , facts : AutoFacts , names : Iterable [ str ]) -> dict [ str , tuple [ str , ... ]] Map each new name to the automatic glyphs that FontLab may rebuild when it appears. A candidate owns a layer with autoLayer and no own recipe (a default-recipe automatic layer), and its name shares a whole dotted suffix segment with the new name ( e.sc and eacute.sc ; not x.scale ). A new name without a dot gets no candidates. Names without candidates are left out. Only the owners in facts.autos are read. Scope: this is a pre-write HEURISTIC for the consent tick, not a prediction. Adding ANY glyph re-resolves every automatic layer of the font: Add Glyph passes every glyph id to _process_update_auto_layers ( flhistorycontroller.cpp:1910-1921 ) and UpdatePackageData::updateAutoLayers walks every auto layer ( update_components.cpp:716-790 ). So any new name, dotted or not ( acute and Aacute ), can change any default-recipe automatic glyph. The guard is the after-write auto_changes check. This is a reading of the source, not a measurement.
title: fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.auto_candidates

text: create_glyphs ( package : Any , specs : Sequence [ NewGlyph ], title : str , facts : AutoFacts , * , fill : Callable [[ dict [ str , Any ]], None ] | None = None , read_back : Callable [[], Iterable [ str ]] | None = None , allow_rebuild : bool = False ) -> Created Create every glyph of specs , then optionally fill them in ONE Undo step. facts : a fresh history.scan_auto_facts(package) . fill(glyphs) gets {name: new package glyph} and edits the new master layers (find them with glyph.findLayer(master) ); it runs inside one history.commit(title, layers, glyphs, ..., operation="geometry") that declares every new layer and glyph. read_back() returns one text per mismatch with the plan. allow_rebuild : the user ticked REBUILD_LABEL ; it also goes to the commit as allow_bases . Raise ValueError before any change for a refusal (module text, step 1). When FontLab refuses the FIRST glyph before its command runs, raise RuntimeError ("... did not start ... No glyph was added.") without the Undo hint. Every other failure raises history.PartialWriteError (with history.UNDO_HINT ); after the first glyph exists its text names the new glyphs. text: Find the upper- or lowercase counterparts of the selected glyphs and select them. What it does: Counterparts come from Unicode case mapping of each glyph's code point; unencoded alternates use their base name (a.ss01 -> A.ss01). Select the counterparts alone or together with the originals. Nothing in the font changes. How it works: Map Unicode case counterparts to existing glyphs. For unencoded suffixed names, try the base counterpart with the original suffix; reject multi- character case expansions. Why this design: A Unicode case change is not always one glyph, so missing or expanding mappings remain visible rather than guessed. How to use: Select source glyphs and run Names > Case Pairs. Review the mapping rows, choose whether originals stay selected and select the available counterparts. Benefit: Move between related case glyphs while preserving names, encodings and outlines.

text: Paste a text or a character set and compare it with the font's encoded characters. What it does: Lists characters of the text the font lacks and characters the font has that the text does not use, with names from unicodedata. Language presets fill in common alphabets. Copy the missing set, or select the extra glyphs in the Font window. Nothing in the font changes. How it works: Compare distinct non-whitespace input characters with every encoded font character. Show missing and extra sets with Unicode names and code points. Why this design: A character-set comparison answers a repertoire question without confusing unencoded alternates with encoded characters. How to use: Run Names > Character Set Compare. Paste text or choose a language preset, inspect both lists, then copy missing characters or select extra glyphs as required. Benefit: Prepare a character-coverage review while leaving encodings and glyph membership intact.

text: Preview style linking for the exportable instances of the current font. What: Link whole-word Bold, Italic and Oblique styles to an available base. Width groups remain separate. ExtraBold and SemiBold are not Bold. How: A non-modal table previews FontLab style-group names and link flags. Apply obtains fresh instance values and changes only matching rows. The package owns instance values; assign the complete instance list back. Notifications follow FontLab Font Info: package and masters container before assignment, then the same list after assignment. Why: FontLab uses a style-group name and bold/italic flags instead of Glyphs linkStyle. Native autoSLV/autoSGN and the Instances multi-select controls already set these values. This tool adds whole-word base matching across width groups in one preview. Per-instance family names (tfn) can differ from the font family and are not exposed by the Python instance API. Therefore an automatic base group is kept: set that base group explicitly in Font Info first. Only explicit base groups are copied. Instance family names and other hidden properties stay in the native value objects. Use: Open a font with instances. Run this tool, check the table, then Apply. Refresh reads the current font again. Close releases owned signals. Benefit: Preview regular/bold/italic relationships across the complete family. Credit: Giuseppe Salerno / Resistenza Type, StyleLinker.py, https://github.com/rsztype/Scripts, Apache-2.0. Independent behaviour-only rewrite. No source code was copied.

text: A live panel describing the character of the glyph selected in the Font window. What it does: Shows the outline next to the system font's rendering, the code point, the Unicode name and category (Python's unicodedata), case counterpart, decomposition and the UTF-8/UTF-16 encodings. It follows the selection twice a second; nothing in the font changes. How it works: Describe the selected glyph's encoded character with Python Unicode data. Draw its current outline beside a system-font character and refresh from the live selection. Why this design: The separate renderings distinguish character identity from the font's own drawing without treating the system glyph as a design target. How to use: Run Names > Character Info. Select an encoded glyph in the Font window, inspect its code point and encodings and use Copy to copy the current character. Benefit: Check Unicode identity, case and decomposition while leaving the glyph's encoding unchanged.
title: fontlabapp.glyphs.identity_tools.glyph_browser.character_info

text: Type to find glyphs by name, character or code point; Enter selects them in the Font window. What it does: Accepts a name fragment (acute), a wildcard pattern (*.ss0?), a character (é), or a code point (U+00E9, 0x1E82, uni00E9). The list updates as you type; double-click a row to select just that glyph. Nothing in the font changes. How it works: Choose a matcher from the query syntax: name fragment, wildcard, literal character or code-point form. Filter glyph records and guard explicit Font-window selection. Why this design: Several input forms let the user locate an encoded character or a named alternate in the same view. How to use: Run Names > Glyph Finder. Enter a query, inspect the result list and press Enter to select matches. Double-click a row when only that glyph is required. Benefit: Find glyphs by the identifier at hand without renaming or changing their Unicode assignments.

text: Browse every glyph of the current font as an expandable metadata tree. What: Opens a modeless panel with one top-level row per glyph, in font order. Expand a glyph to see each Unicode value assigned to it and the local date when the glyph was last modified. Glyphs without a Unicode value say "Not encoded"; glyphs without a recorded date say "Not recorded". A glyph with several Unicode values lists every one of them. Use: Open a font. Run Names > Glyph Metadata Tree. Expand the glyphs you want to inspect. Press Refresh after you change the font; the panel does not follow edits by itself. Close the panel when you are done. If no font is open, or the font changes while the panel reads it, the panel status line says so and shows no partial tree. Safety: Read-only. The tool reads glyph names, Unicode values and modification dates once per refresh. It writes no font data, selection, history, preference, clipboard or Output text. Closing the panel releases only the widgets that the panel created. Source: Original workflow built on the shared App glyph tree (fontlabapp.glyphs.tree.model), Apache-2.0. Requires App>=1.2.0 and fontlab-fly in FontLab 9 Python 3.11.

text: Draft text with completions taken from the glyph names of the current font. What: Opens a modeless panel with a text area. As you type, the panel offers the exact glyph names of the current font as completions, so you can write lists of glyph names (for a class, a test string or a note) without typos. Typing at least three characters, or pressing Ctrl+E, opens the completion list. The vocabulary is the complete glyph-name list in font order. Use: Open a font. Run Names > Glyph Name Completion. Type a draft and pick names from the list. Press Refresh to reload the vocabulary after the font changed; your draft stays. Select and copy the text with the normal text shortcuts. Close the panel when you are done. The draft is not saved anywhere. Safety: The panel only reads glyph names. Your draft lives in the panel and is lost when the panel closes. The tool writes no font data, selection, history, preference, file or Output text, and it never copies text by itself. Standard text selection and copy stay under your control. Source: Original workflow built on the shared App completion panel (fontlabapp.glyphs.completion.model), Apache-2.0. Requires App>=1.2.0 and fontlab-fly in FontLab 9 Python 3.11.

text: Find and replace in glyph names, with a live preview and strict checks. WHAT: A non-modal panel takes a Find text (plain or regular expression) and a Replace text. It lists every glyph whose name would change, with the new name and a check result. Rename applies all rows that pass. HOW: The script scans the font on open and on Reload, and again before the write. A row passes only when the new name is valid, does not exist, is not the target of another row, and the glyph is not tied to an auto layer. The write is one Undo step. The rename uses the font-owned FontGate record, never flGlyph.fgGlyph. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: FontLab would replace an existing glyph that has the new name, so the script refuses that. FontLab rebuilds auto layers when they are notified (it turned ecircumflex into a lone "ee" after e was renamed). So the script REFUSES glyphs that have auto layers and glyphs that are the base of an auto composite, also through other composites. It never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537) and refuses to hide queued ids; it discloses their possible date changes. Kerning and features keep the old names. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Type Find and Replace. Use \1 for groups in regular-expression mode. Press Rename. Choose "All glyphs" to rename across the font. BENEFIT: Bulk renames (for example uniXXXX to AGL names) are safe, previewed and reversible with one Edit > Undo. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

text: Find shared Unicode assignments across the whole current font and remove chosen pairs. Expanded codepoint groups preserve font order and prefer the first primary owner as keeper. Untick any row to keep its code, or tick the keeper too. Rescan resets the preview; Remove ticked writes only the checked assignments and refreshes. Requires Fly and App1.2.0. No glyph geometry or selection is edited. Close all Glyph editors and activate the Font window before applying. Changed sources, pending native glyph updates, automatic targets/dependants or surviving repeated-code lists that the native setter would collapse refuse before history. One final history batch is used; a partial failure diagnoses Edit > Undo. Full native history/font/reopen preservation remains unqualified; no UpdateAll or fgGlyph conversion is used.

text: Add, remove or replace a glyph-name suffix (.ss01, .sc, .alt) on the selected glyphs. WHAT: A non-modal panel offers three operations. Add puts a suffix on each selected name. Remove strips one suffix (or the last suffix when the field is empty). Replace swaps one suffix for another. A table previews every new name and a check result. Apply renames all rows that pass. HOW: The script rescans the font before the write. A row passes only when the new name is valid, does not exist, is not the target of another row, and the glyph is not tied to an auto layer. The write is one Undo step. The rename and the optional Unicode removal use the font-owned FontGate record, never flGlyph.fgGlyph. After clearing Unicode the script reads the list back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: Suffixed alternates are normally unencoded, so the panel can clear their Unicode in the same step. FontLab would replace an existing glyph that has the new name, so the script refuses that. FontLab rebuilds auto layers when they are notified, so the script REFUSES glyphs that have auto layers and glyphs that are the base of an auto composite, also through other composites. It never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537) and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. Before it removes Unicode, the script applies the guards of the App Unicode writer: a regular Font window must be active and no Glyph editor may be open. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose the operation, type or pick a suffix (a missing leading dot is added), then press Apply. BENEFIT: Alternate sets (.ss01, .sc, .case) get consistent names in one previewed, undoable step. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

text: Assign Unicode code points that the glyph names imply. Preview first. WHAT: A non-modal panel reads glyph names and lists the code point each name implies. It knows uniXXXX and uXXXX[XX] names, a built-in table of Adobe Glyph List names, and accented Latin names (Wacute is LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W WITH ACUTE, found with unicodedata). Names with a suffix (a.ss01), ligature names (f_i) and surrogate code points (U+D800 to U+DFFF) are left alone. Assign writes all rows marked "assign". HOW: The script scans the font and plans each row: "same" (already right), "encoded differently" (the glyph has another code and Replace is off), "used by X" (another glyph already owns the code, or an earlier row claims it), a refusal reason, or "assign". The write rescans, then sets the code points on the font-owned FontGate record as one Undo step. It reads each list back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: A code point must belong to one glyph only. The plan never steals a code from another glyph and never lets two rows claim one code. FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer, or the base glyph of an auto composite (also through other composites), is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES such glyphs. It never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph, never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. Before it writes, the script applies the guards of the App Unicode writer: a regular Font window must be active and no Glyph editor may be open. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window, or choose "All glyphs in the font". Run the script. Check the table. Press Assign. BENEFIT: Fonts built from named outlines get a correct character map in one previewed, undoable step. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

text: Set or append one note on every selected glyph at once. WHAT: A non-modal panel takes a note text and an operation. Set replaces each glyph note (an empty Set clears the notes). Append adds the text on a new line after the existing note. A table shows every note before and after. Apply writes only the glyphs whose note changes. HOW: The script reads the selection through the shared App selection reader and scans the whole font. For the write it rescans, plans, and writes as one Undo step: layers and glyph in one notify list (a glyph alone adds no Undo step). After the write it reads each note back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: A glyph note belongs to the glyph, not to a master. FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES glyphs that own an auto layer, shows the reason in the table, and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may get a note (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph (that getter can clear a fresh note mirror on build 9784), never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Choose Set or Append, type the note, check the table, press Apply. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. BENEFIT: Review comments or to-do remarks reach many glyphs in one undoable step, with a preview. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.
title: fontlabapp.glyphs.identity_tools.glyph_labels.batch_glyph_notes

text: Read and edit the note of one glyph. Browse every glyph that has a note. WHAT: A non-modal panel shows the note of the first glyph selected in the Font window in an editor. Save writes it. A list below shows all glyphs that have a note. A click loads that note into the editor. A double-click also selects the glyph in the Font window. HOW: The script scans the whole font. Save rescans, then writes one note as one Undo step: layers and glyph in one notify list (a glyph alone adds no Undo step). It then reads the note back and compares it with the text. Double-click selection goes through the App selection helper, which checks that a regular Font window is active (fl#8528). The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified, and Undo does not restore them. So the script REFUSES to save a note on a glyph that owns an auto layer, says why, and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may get a note (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph (that getter can clear a fresh note mirror on build 9784), never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537), and discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. USE: Select a glyph in the Font window. Run the script. Edit the note. Press Save note. Pick a row in the list to edit another glyph. BENEFIT: Notes travel with the glyph in .vfc and .vfj files. The list gives an overview of all remarks in the font. One Edit > Undo reverts one save. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. text: Add tags to, or remove tags from, the selected glyphs in one step. WHAT: A non-modal panel lists each tag used by the selected glyphs and how many glyphs carry it. Type a tag and press Add, or tick tags and press Remove. The tag field completes from all tags in the font. HOW: The script reads the selection through the shared App selection reader. It then scans the whole font once. For each edit it rescans, builds a plan, and writes the plan as one Undo step. After the write it reads each tag list back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified. Undo does not restore the rebuilt layers. So the script REFUSES glyphs that own an auto layer and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may be tagged: its tags do not reach the composites (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph (that getter can clear a fresh glyph note on build 9784). It never calls UpdateAll (that feeds the fl#8537 pending-update queue). It discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. A tag has 1 to 64 characters, no spaces and no commas. BENEFIT: Review states, spacing status and similar marks stay on the glyphs and travel with the font. One Edit > Undo reverts one Add or Remove. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

It then reads each mark back and compares it with the plan. The scan, the refusal policy and the one-step write come from the shared module fontlabapp.glyphs.names.model. If a write fails part way, every planned glyph is still notified and stamped, and the message asks you to use Edit > Undo. WHY: FontLab rebuilds all auto layers when an auto layer is notified. Undo does not restore the rebuilt layers. So the script REFUSES glyphs that own an auto layer and never puts an auto layer in the notify list. A base glyph of an auto composite may be marked: its mark does not reach the composites (native check pending). The script never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph, never calls UpdateAll (fl#8537) discloses queued ids and their possible date changes. Swatch colours come from plain HLS arithmetic, so the colour logic works and is testable without Qt. USE: Select glyphs in the Font window. Run the script. Click a swatch. Press Reload selection after you change the selection. BENEFIT: Colour marks sort work (done, check, kerning needed) and show in the Font window. One Edit > Undo reverts one click. Credit: adapted from the author's own archived Apache-2.0 FontLab samples. The edit is recorded as one Undo step.

text: Select glyphs in the Font window by their mark colour. What it does: Lists every mark colour used in the font (and unmarked glyphs) with a swatch and a count. Why this design: Colour groups can identify a work batch without requiring a persistent naming convention. How to use: Run Names > Select by Mark.
